key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection offers a route to more stable perovskite devices, alongside surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Assessed environmental photo- and thermal stability.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, but PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no device-efficiency or lifetime metrics, so improved material stability does not establish long-term solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
